full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J: This Rule obtained u/s. 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure arises out of a suit for cancellation of the deed of gift dated 5.1.76 purported to have been executed by the plaintiff opposite party in favour of the defendant petitioner No. 1 and also for a declaration that the registered kabala dated 5.1.76 executed by the defendant petitioner No. 1 in favour of the defendant petitioner No. 2 is void ab initio and illegal. The learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Rangpur by his judgment and order dated 73.7.79 in O.S. No. 349/77 dismissed the suit. On appeal, the learned Subordinate Judge, Rangpur by his judgment and Order dated 7.4.80 in Other Appeal No. 133/79 allowed the same and decreed the suit of the plaintiff opposite party. 

 5. The appellate court below also concurred with the findings of the trial court that there was no fraud in the execution and registration of the deed of gift. On the question of the possession of the petitioner No 1, the appellate court below held that even if it is conceded that the petitioner No. 1 possessed the suit land that cannot amount to possession in his own right. He must be deemed to have been in possession on behalf of the plaintiff because admittedly the petitioner No. 1 used to look after her properties, Dakhilas Ext. 3 series also show that the plaintiff paid rent for the suit land by two dakhilas dated 26.11.77 after the alleged deed of gift. The appellate court below held that the plaintiff has not parted with here possession of the suit land. As such the gift was not complete. Hence the appellate court below allowed the appeal and decreed the plaintiff's suit. 

 The judgment and decree of the appellate court below, therefore, cannot be sustained. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute but without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree of the appellate court below are set aside and those of the trial court are affirmed.
